statement: The ET-SoC-1 has 1,093 RISC-V cores: 1,088 ET-Minions, 4 ET-Maxions and 1 Minion-based service processor.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 (§1 Product Overview); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.7 (§1)

statement: 34 minion shires of 32 minions each = 1,088 minions. The hierarchy figure describes '34 Shires / 1,088 Minion cores and 4 Maxion cores in a 6 x 6 array'; with the PCIe and I/O shires (the Maxions sit in the I/O shire) that fills the 36 cells.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1) and Figure 2-1 on pdf p.6; external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.8-9 (§1.2, Figure 1-1)

statement: 1,088 minions on the chip (34 shires × 32).
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.15 (§2.2.1)

statement: Typically 32 minion shires form the compute array and one more is the management (master) shire; the datasheet calls this a software convention, all minion shires being identical. The 34th is a yield-recovery spare, powered down in production.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.486 (§15.3: 'the 34th shire will be designated as a powered down yield recovery spare')

statement: Kernels in these measurements run on 1,024 minions: the 32 compute shires × 32.
The driver reports compute shire mask 0xffffffff (shires 0-31) and sync (master) shire 32 on every card.
page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

statement: Software sees 2,048 harts on the 32 compute shires: hartid = shire × 64 + minion × 2 + thread (shire = hartid >> 6, neighbourhood = (hartid mod 64) >> 4, minion = hartid >> 1, thread = hartid & 1).
The master shire (which runs the master-minion firmware and schedules kernels) is shire 32 in the firmware; its 2.5 MB scratchpad at 0x9000_0000 holds the firmware's host-interface buffers.
note: layout.h:45 also reserves MASTER_SHIRE_COMPUTE_HARTS 32; minion_configuration.h:53 MM_MASTER_SHIRE_NEIGH_NUM 2.

statement: The spare shire is bit 33 of the firmware's 34-shire mask; the NoC reconfiguration code remaps virtual shire IDs when the spare displaces a shire.
Four ET-Maxion 64-bit RISC-V single-threaded superscalar out-of-order cores sit in the I/O shire with a system bus and coherency hub; they may be used for management tasks.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 (§1) and pdf p.18 (§2.5.2)

statement: The service processor is a single ET-Minion core (one hart, no vector or tensor extension, no shire cache) in the I/O shire, with its own ROM and 1 MB scratchpad SRAM; it boots the chip, runs the power/clock governor and answers the host's management commands.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1) and pdf p.18 (§2.4); external/et-man/ET Introduction.pdf, pdf p.7 ('Service Processor is a minion without vector/tensor extensions')
page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

statement: The I/O shire holds the Maxion neighbourhood (4 Maxions) with a shared L2/L3 cache, the service processor with ROM and 1 MB SRAM, a hardware root of trust, five PVT controllers and the peripherals (USB, I2C, SPI, UART, eMMC).
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.17 (§1.6, PVT controllers in the I/O shire)
note: Sources disagree on the Maxions' cache: the datasheet (pdf p.5) and PRM (pdf p.486) say 4 MB; the Shire Cache Specification (pdf p.22) says 'the IOShire has a cache total of 1 MB'.

statement: The PCIe shire contains two independent dual-mode PCIe controllers and an 8-lane PCIe Gen4 PHY, factory-configured as an endpoint; the dev card exposes a Gen4 x8 host interface.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1) and pdf p.17 (§2.3, Figure 2-7)

statement: Eight memory shires, four on the east side and four on the west side of the die, each driving two 16-bit LPDDR4X channels: 16 channels in all.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.30 (§7); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.17 (§1.5)

statement: 140 MB of on-die SRAM (35 shire caches × 4 MB, counting the I/O shire's), each 1 MB block configurable as local L2, a slice of the chip-wide L3, or globally addressable scratchpad.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 (§1); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.486 (§15.3)
note: The I/O shire's cache is 1 MB in the Shire Cache Specification (pdf p.22), which would make it 137 MB.

statement: TSMC 7 nm, over 24 billion transistors, 89 mask layers (Esperanto, Hot Chips 33 and IEEE Micro 2022).
note: External, published by the vendor; not checked on these cards.

statement: Die area 570 mm².
source: docs/findings/05-claims.md:513; docs/findings/01-resources.md:234 (R14: Hot Chips 33 slide 20; IEEE Micro 42(3) p.37)
note: External, vendor-published.

statement: Die about 25.6-25.8 mm east-west by 22.1-22.2 mm north-south (width/height 1.15-1.17), from the published die plot scaled to 570 mm²; the shire grid spans about 86% of the die's width, the rest being the memory shires and their DRAM PHYs down each side (about 1.76 mm per side).
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/geometry/pitch.json, `scale_from_570mm2.A_black_layout_region` and `.B_symmetric_bottom` (`die_w_mm`, `die_h_mm`, `grid_w_mm`, `memshire_col_w_mm`); heat-per-mm page §'How long is a hop'
note: Pixel measurement of a die plot; depends on what the 570 mm² covers. Use for proportions only.

statement: Shire tile pitch 3.73 mm east-west and 3.70 mm north-south, so one mesh hop is about 3.72 mm (3.64-3.74 over three readings).
note: Kind A (estimate from the die plot) in the claims index.

statement: The datasheet's package marking example gives die revision A0; the driver reports arch_rev 0 on every card. Whether the lab cards are A0 has not been confirmed by AI Foundry.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.34 (Table 10-1); docs/reports/data/2026-09-22-cards/driver_config.json `arch_rev`; docs/et-soc1-notes.md:342

statement: Advertised operating range: 300-800 MHz and about 40 W for the open-sourced platform (AI Foundry); Esperanto's papers give 300 MHz to 2 GHz.
note: These cards' firmware only offers 600, 700 and 800 MHz (see clock.minion-opps).

statement: The NoC is an 8 × 6 grid of mesh stops: 34 minion shires, 1 PCIe shire, 1 I/O shire and 8 memory shires; the four memory shires on each side leave the grid's corners empty, so there are 44 mesh stops.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.21 (§4 ET-SoC-1 Mesh Network on Chip)

statement: Measured position of each compute shire on the 6 × 6 grid (marty1885's logical map, x across, y down): y=0: 0 24 9 25 2 11; y=1: 8 16 1 17 10 19; y=2: 3 4 13 14 18 27; y=3: _ 12 21 22 26 _; y=4: _ 20 29 30 15 23; y=5: _ 28 5 6 7 31.
source: workloads/nocbench/analyze.py:52-60 (`MARTY`, `EMPTY`); docs/findings/05-claims.md:383, 412 (map recovered from latency alone in 12 of 12 search restarts on every card)
note: Built by marty1885's etTopoScan from bandwidth on another card; confirmed by TensorSend latency on all three lab cards. Shire IDs are the firmware's logical IDs.

statement: Four cells of the 6 × 6 map hold no compute shire: (0,3), (0,4), (0,5) and (5,3). They hold the master, spare, PCIe and I/O shires and route traffic too; which cell is which is not established.
source: workloads/nocbench/analyze.py:60 (`EMPTY`); on-chip communication page §'Where the shires are'
note: The firmware's comment map (noc_reconfigure.h:76-90) puts PCIe/IO in one row and master/spare in another, but its shire placement matches the measured pairwise distances for only 254 of 1,024 shire pairs, so it cannot be used to label the cells.

statement: The logical map appears to be the die turned a quarter: in map orientation the memory shires sit above and below the grid, on the die (and in the firmware's naming, 0-3 west, 4-7 east) they are the two side columns.

Fitted memory-shire positions on the logical map: memory shires 0-3 one step off the top edge at x = 1-4 (y = -1), 4-7 one step off the bottom edge at x = 1-4 (y = 6). Memory shire 2's position is a tie-break (x = 3 or 5 above the grid, or (6,0), fit equally).
note: A fit of DRAM latencies with one constant (91 cycles) and 12 cycles per hop.

statement: Fitted memory-shire positions (x = 1-4 in the rows above and below the 6 × 6 grid) leave exactly the four corner stops of the 8 × 6 grid empty, as the datasheet says; together they give 44 stops.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json `decomp.ms_pos`; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.21 (§4)

statement: L3 hit latency from shire 0 to each of the 32 home slices is exactly 110 + 12 × hops for 0 to 10 hops (110, 122, ... 230 cycles), the median of every pass on each of three cards.
note: Per-slice data the diagram can animate from directly (requester shire 0).

statement: A ring through all 32 compute shires moving one hop per step: 0 24 9 25 2 11 19 27 18 10 17 14 22 26 15 23 31 7 6 30 29 5 28 20 12 21 13 1 16 4 3 8 (then back to 0).
source: docs/et-soc1-notes.md:108-109; on-chip communication page §'Where the shires are'

statement: Shire IDs do not follow the mesh: the next shire by ID is 1-10 hops away, 3.5 on average.
page: Hand it to the next shire: on-chip relay vs DRAM

statement: Each mesh hop adds 20 ns round trip: 12 minion cycles at 600 MHz (11.99-12.02 fitted on three cards), about 4 mesh cycles each way at 400 MHz, the same in both directions.
unit: minion cycles per hop (round trip, 600 MHz)
note: Fixed in ns, so 16 cycles at 800 MHz.

statement: Round trips fit a + b × Manhattan distance on the map over all 496 shire pairs (worst residual 1.1-1.4 cycles), so routes are shortest paths through all 36 cells, the four non-compute cells included. The order in which the mesh routes a request (x first or y first) was not measured.
source: docs/findings/05-claims.md:381, 412; on-chip communication page §'What the numbers say'; anatomy page §1 ('the order in which the mesh routes a request was not measured')

statement: The heat-per-mm analysis assumes dimension-ordered XY routing on the logical map (and checks YX); under it, links are shared by 0 / 22 / 32 / 55 / 72% of link-hops at 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 6 hops in the all-pairs traffic.
note: An analysis assumption, not a documented routing rule.

statement: Each shire meets the mesh at a single point: minion 31 of each shire gives the same round trips as minion 0.
source: on-chip communication page §'What the numbers say'

statement: The NoC runs at 400 MHz on these cards (every telemetry sample). The design's NoC clock is 500 MHz (from PLL2 in the I/O shire), and the firmware's DVFS table allows 300-500 MHz.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace-telemetry.jsonl (and horace2-, thermal-telemetry.jsonl: 3,681 samples, 20 Sep), field `mhz.noc`; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.12 (Table 2, clk__noc); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/services/thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:134-135
card: aifoundry2 (aifoundry3 set to 400 MHz by its boot service)

statement: NoC rail: set point 485 mV, 484-485 mV on die (per-shire 483-486 mV at idle).
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace-telemetry.jsonl (and horace2-, thermal-telemetry.jsonl: 3,681 samples, 20 Sep), fields `reg_mv.noc`, `die_mv.noc`; docs/findings/05-claims.md:41

statement: The shire cache's mesh master port is 512 bits wide (one 64-byte line per beat); a shire has four mesh lanes and a line goes to lane PA[7:6], so consecutive lines on one lane are 256 bytes apart; a flit carries at least one 64-byte line.
note: The inter-router link width and flit size of the NoC itself are not documented in the sources.

statement: Each memory shire has three NoC ports (memory traffic, global-atomic responses, ESR accesses); the memory port is a 512-bit AXI slave, and the NoC delivers at most 32 GB/s to a memory shire, almost twice the sustained rate of its two LPDDR4X channels.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.30 (§7.1.1)

statement: With 1 KB messages a round trip adds 12 cycles per hop up to 5 hops and 36 cycles (27-36) per hop beyond, as if the sender had a limited number of packets in flight.
One mesh hop costs 0.67 pJ per byte on zeros [0.62-0.73] and 1.80 pJ/B on random data [1.72-1.91] on board power (fit over 1-8 hops).

A random bit moved one mm across the mesh costs 37 fJ on the mesh rail (25 of it data-dependent) and 47 fJ on board power when links are free (0.485 V); 53 and 79 fJ on a loaded mesh where flows share links.
unit: fJ per bit·mm (mesh rail, free links)
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/report.json `headline["uncontended/noc_rail"|"uncontended/board"|"loaded/noc_rail"|"loaded/board"].random_bit_total`; docs/findings/20-heat-per-mm.md:9-12; docs/findings/05-claims.md:444 (V3 free links per card)

statement: A separate Debug NoC shares the main NoC's clock with its own reset.
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.7 (Table 1) and pdf p.17

statement: There are no NoC performance counters in the PRM, the firmware or core-et; mesh transit is inferred from latency differences.

A minion shire is 4 neighbourhoods = 32 minions = 64 harts, a four-bank 4 MB shared L2/L3/scratchpad cache, a mesh stop, a crossbar between them, and an uncacheable (UC) block with fast local barriers, fast credit counters, inter-processor interrupts and global atomics.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1); external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.4 (slide 5)

statement: The shire cache is 4 MB: 4 banks × 1 MB, each bank 4 sub-banks; L2 and L3 are 4-way set-associative, 64-byte lines, write-back and write-allocate, with SECDED ECC on tags, data and state.
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.8-9 (§1.1: 'The POR for the first SoC is 4M/Shire, 4 banks/Shire, 4 sub-banks/bank'); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.13 (§2.1.3.1)

statement: Mode M0, the reset mode and the one these cards run: per shire 2.5 MB scratchpad, 512 KB L2, 1 MB L3 slice; over 32 shires 80 MB scratchpad, 16 MB L2, 32 MB L3.
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.21-22 (Tables 6-7, 'The chip will come out of reset in mode M0'); external/core-et/rtl/shire/esr/esr_cache_bank.v:106 ('default cache config mode = M0'); external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.4

statement: The driver reports L2 16,384 KB, L3 32,768 KB and scratchpad 81,920 KB in total on every card, i.e. mode M0; line size 64 B, 4 L2 banks.
Other defined partitions (chip totals, scratchpad / L2 / L3): M1 0/64/64 MB, M2 0/124/4, M3 0/128/0, M4 128/0/0, M5 64/64/0; software can change mode only after evicting and stopping the minions.

A full request crossbar joins the 4 neighbourhoods and the RBOX to the 4 banks and the UC block; each bank has five 512-bit L2 input ET-Link buses, one 512-bit L3 input bus from the NoC, and two outputs toward the NoC: 'To L3' and 'To System' (main memory).
The 8 minions of a neighbourhood share one 512-bit ET-Link bus to the shire cache and UC block; responses reach a minion over a 256-bit bus (a 512-bit line takes two cycles).
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.11 (§3.2); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.22-23

statement: Idle shire-cache latencies in shire clocks, crossbars included: read-buffer hit 10, L2 read hit 21, L2 miss 34 + NoC and L3/memory, L3 read hit 30 (at the slave), L3 miss 42 + NoC and memory.
note: Measured load-to-use is 36 (read buffer) and 47 (L2) minion cycles; the difference is the minion pipeline, L1 miss and neighbourhood path.

statement: Per bank: a 64-entry request queue (up to 21 entries reserved for L3-slave requests), an 8-entry read buffer and a 32-entry write-around coalescing buffer; L3-slave requests take priority over local L2 requests.
source: docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:458-465; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.9 (coalescing buffer, 32 entries per bank) and pdf p.36 (arbitration)
page: One hot line stops a shire

statement: Spec L2 bandwidth: four banks × 64 B = 256 B per shire-cycle, i.e. 8 B per minion-cycle, 4.9 TB/s on 1,024 minions at 600 MHz.
Measured L2 streaming bandwidth: 2.45 TB/s on 1,024 minions at 600 MHz = 128 B per shire-cycle = 4.0 B per minion-cycle, half the banks' 256 B.
card: aifoundry2 (re-run on aifoundry2 and aifoundry3 on 23 Sep, within 1%)

statement: Each minion shire has its own PLL; the shire cache and minions run on the shire clock (the neighbourhood clock is the same clock shifted 180°), outside the NoC's clock domain. Design value 1,000 MHz.
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.4 and pdf p.12 (Table 2: o_clkpll_shire, o_clkpll_neigh)
note: Measured consequence: on-chip latencies (L1, L2, own scratchpad) stay fixed in cycles when the clock moves, while L3 and DRAM are fixed in ns.

statement: A shire spans several voltage domains separated by level shifters and FIFOs: minions on the low-voltage minion rail, the SRAM arrays (shire cache, and the I-cache data memory, placed in the shire channel because it must run at high voltage) on the SRAM rail, the mesh stop on the NoC rail.
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.4, p.10 (§3.1) and p.18 (§5); docs/research/why-low-power.md:23-28 (R6)

statement: One temperature sensor and one process detector per minion shire (plus the I/O shire), and 3 voltage sense points per minion shire; the host sees only the mean temperature of the 34 minion-shire sensors, in whole degrees.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.17 (§1.6: 36 TS and 36 PD); docs/findings/01-resources.md:212-215 (R13: 35 live); docs/findings/05-claims.md:36, 331
note: The PRM counts 36 sensors of each kind; the firmware has 35 live (34 minion shires + I/O shire). Per-shire temperature is not exported.

statement: A neighbourhood is 8 minions sharing a 32 KB L1 instruction cache (128 sets × 4 ways × 64 B), two L0 micro-I-caches (each shared by 4 minions, 16 fully associative 512-bit entries) and a 12-counter PMU.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.11-13 (§2.1.2); external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.3 (slide 4)

statement: The neighbourhood PMU implements 12 counters: 6 shared by the even harts (hart 0 of each minion) and 6 by the odd harts; mcycle and minstret read 0.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.10 and p.12 (§1.3, §1.3.2)

statement: The fast local messaging network links minions within a neighbourhood only along the reduction tree: 0-1, 0-2, 0-4, 2-3, 4-5, 4-6, 6-7.
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.26 (§4.7 Fast Local Messaging Network)

statement: A 32 B TensorSend round trip takes 68 cycles (113 ns) on a fast-network edge (28 pairs per shire) and 114-115 cycles (190 ns) between any other two minions of a shire, same neighbourhood or not.

Messages on the fast local network see a 3-cycle response-path latency and take priority over regular fill responses; every other message leaves the neighbourhood and returns through the shire crossbar.

Cooperative TensorLoad: identical tensor-load requests from minions (across the neighbourhoods of a shire) are synchronised and coalesced into one memory request; cooperative TensorStore combines pairs or quads of minions writing one line.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.273-274 (§9.3.1.1, §9.3.5.1); external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.3

statement: Two page-table walkers per neighbourhood are drawn in the architecture but not implemented in the first silicon revision.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.11 (footnote 1)

statement: The ET-Minion is a dual-threaded (2 harts), in-order, single-issue RV64IMFC core with Zicsr and Zifencei and machine/supervisor/user modes; kernels run in U-mode.
source: external/core-et/docs/Minion Description.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.7 (§2.1.1); external/et-man/ET Introduction.pdf, pdf p.7

statement: No hardware divide or square root in U-mode: fdiv.ps and fsqrt.ps trap, as do sine, reciprocal square root, 64-bit float conversion and reading the cycle CSR; 161 of the instructions tried execute in U-mode, 13 trap.

The vector unit has 8 identical 32-bit lanes in lockstep; the 32 FP registers f0-f31 are 256 bits wide (8 × fp32) per hart. Each lane has one FMA unit (one fp32 or two fp16 multiply-adds per cycle), two integer multiply-add units (four int8 multiply-accumulates each), one integer unit and one transcendental unit (exp2, log2, reciprocal).
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.8 (§2.1.1.2); external/core-et/docs/Minion VPU Specification.pdf, pdf p.11 (§2) and p.33 (§2.2.5.2: 16 TIMA lanes); external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.2 (slide 3)

statement: Each lane's register file holds 64 × 32-bit entries (32 per thread), so each hart has 32 vector registers of 32 bytes; 8 mask registers of 8 bits.
unit: vector registers per hart (32 B each)
source: external/core-et/docs/Minion VPU Specification.pdf, pdf p.11; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.8-9

statement: The VPU pipeline has eight stages.
The data cache can feed one register-file entry of all 8 VPU lanes (32 bytes) in a single cycle.
Tensor peak per minion-cycle: 16 fp32 FLOP, 32 fp16 FLOP, 128 int8 OP (int8 is 8× fp32 because the integer units are separate and twice as many).
Chip tensor peak on 1,024 minions at 600 MHz: 9.83 TFLOP/s fp32, 19.7 TFLOP/s fp16, 78.6 TOP/s int8.

A tensor-unit matmul on 1,024 minions at 600 MHz sustains 9.51 TFLOP/s fp32, 19.02 fp16 and 71.77 TOP/s int8: 529 cycles per 16×16×K op for fp32/fp16 (512 ideal) and 280.4 for int8 (256 ideal), every result exact.
With A and B both in the L1 scratchpad a 16×16×16 fp32 TensorFMA takes 546 cycles (fp16 546, int8 318), identical for every data pattern.

A TensorFMA computes C[M][N] += A[M][K] · B[K][N] with M, N ≤ 16 and K ≤ 64 / (bytes per element): A from the L1 scratchpad, B streamed through TenB, C accumulated in hart 0's vector registers (int8 in TenC). One fp32 op is 4,096 multiply-adds.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.264 (§9); docs/et-soc1-notes.md:292-294

statement: TenB is virtually 16 registers × 64 B (1 KiB), physically much smaller, and only streams loaded data to a consumer; TenC is 16 × 64 B (1 KiB) of int32 accumulators visible only to integer tensor multiplies.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.264

statement: Only hart 0 of a minion may issue tensor instructions; hart 1 may only issue TensorLoadL2Scp, TensorWait and tensor_coop accesses.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.264

statement: Tensor instructions are CSR writes that run asynchronously: tensor_fma 0x801, tensor_load 0x83F, tensor_load_l2 (TensorLoadL2Scp) 0x85F, tensor_quant 0x806, tensor_store 0x87F, tensor_reduce 0x800 (TensorSend/Recv/Broadcast/Reduce), tensor_wait 0x830.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.272-274 (§9.3)

statement: TensorLoad reads up to 16 rows of 64 contiguous bytes (64 B aligned, row stride in x31) from memory into consecutive L1-scratchpad lines, bypassing the L1 data cache; a mask can skip rows.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.273 and p.275 (§9.3.1, TensorLoad)

statement: Tensor loads skip the L1 but are cached in the L2 and L3; tensor stores skip the L1 and the L2.
note: Stated by the energy manual; the PRM confirms only that TensorLoad bypasses the L1 data cache.

statement: TensorSend moves COUNT consecutive vector registers (32 B each, up to 127, wrapping past f31: about 4 KB) from the issuing hart into hart 0 of a target minion anywhere on the chip; the receiver's TensorRecv can add, max or min the data into its registers at no extra cost.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.272 and p.311-314; on-chip communication page (headline); docs/findings/05-claims.md:380-381

statement: TensorSend round trip between shires: 150 + 12.02 cycles per mesh hop (250 ns + 20 ns/hop at 600 MHz), r² 0.9999 over all 496 shire pairs.
Combining on receive (fp32/int32 add, max, min) adds 0 cycles to a round trip.
The hardware keeps one peer-to-peer ready bit per minion, not one per partner: a minion receiving from two TensorSend partners at once hangs its hart permanently (the card then needs a reset).
note: sys_emu tracks every partner separately and does not reproduce the hang.

statement: A one-way message stream costs a fixed 40 / 86 / 135 / 224 cycles per message plus 2.3 / 4.0 / 3.0 / 4.6 cycles per 32 B register on the fast network / shire crossbar / mesh at 1 hop / mesh at 10 hops.
source: on-chip communication page §'Message size and bandwidth'

statement: One link with 1 KB messages: 5.3 GB/s on the fast network, 2.9 through the shire crossbar, 2.7 over one mesh hop, 1.8 over ten (4 KB messages: 7.2 / 4.1 / 4.7 / 2.9).
source: on-chip communication page §'Message size and bandwidth'

statement: Each minion has a private 4 KB L1 data cache: 16 sets × 4 ways × 64 B lines, not coherent with any other cache, writing back whole 64-byte lines.
source: external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.1 (slide 2); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.9 (§2.1.1.5)

statement: Three L1 modes (mcache_control D1Split, ScpEnable): shared (both harts, all sets); split (hart 0 sets 0-7, hart 1 sets 14-15); scratchpad (hart 0 sets 12-13, hart 1 sets 14-15, sets 0-11 become a 3 KB = 48-line tensor scratchpad).
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.245-246 (§8.3.1, Table 8.4)
note: The Minion Overview slide draws split mode as 2 KB per hart; the PRM table is followed here.

statement: The firmware puts every minion's L1 in scratchpad mode before each launch, leaving each hart 512 B of data cache (2 sets × 4 ways × 64 B).
Two miss handlers per minion, so at most 2 outstanding cacheable line misses; tensor loads keep up to 4 L2 transfers in flight; there is no prefetcher.
L1 hit: 5.25 cycles load-to-use (8.8 ns at 600 MHz); hart 1 pays 3 more cycles on misses.
L1 bandwidth on 1,024 minions at 600 MHz: 6.2 TB/s in the memory-hierarchy probe's loop, 14.5 TB/s with the catalogue's unrolled 32 B vector loads.
An L1 hit costs 0.75 pJ per byte in the memory-hierarchy loop [0.62-0.88], 0.54 pJ/B on random data with unrolled 32 B loads.
An awake minion running an integer loop on one hart costs about 1.9 mW (both harts about 3.0 mW); on a random-data fp32 matmul a minion draws about 26.5 mW above idle (aifoundry2).
Energy per multiply-add above idle, random operands: fp32 5.78 pJ [5.35-6.13], fp16 2.59, int8 0.295 (TensorFMA); a vector fmadd.ps lane costs 7.0 pJ.
A simple vector-FMA loop reaches only about 1.5 lane-FMAs per cycle per minion; the best published vector-unit matmul is 2.94 TFLOP/s at 650 MHz (FOSDEM 2026), against the tensor unit's 9.5.

The minion's sleep and isolation ports (nsleepin, iso_enable, nsleepout) are marked 'not used'; in the open Erbium RTL they are tied off and no firmware drives them. Idle cores are clock-gated, not power-gated.
source: external/core-et/docs/Minion Description.pdf, pdf p.7 (interfaces table); docs/findings/05-claims.md:177-179
page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

statement: L2 hit (and own-shire scratchpad hit): 47 cycles load-to-use, 78 ns at 600 MHz; L2 read-buffer hit 36 cycles (60 ns). On hart 1 the same loads take 50 and 39 cycles.
Each L2 bank has an 8-line read buffer (2 KB per shire) that serves repeated reads of a clean line without touching the SRAM.
The L2 partition is shared by the 32 minions of its shire and not by other shires: an independent L2 per shire (512 KB; 16 MB chip).
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.13 (§2.1.3.1)

statement: L2 address decode: offset PA[5:0], bank PA[7:6], sub-bank PA[9:8], set from PA[10] up (L2 set bits are PA[19:10] on ET-SoC-1).
Reading from L2 costs 3.1 pJ per byte above idle [1.4-5.0].
Own-shire L2 scratchpad: 47 cycles like L2, 2.46 TB/s on 1,024 minions at 600 MHz, 2.25 pJ/B when it holds zeros and 4.40 pJ/B when it holds random data.

Another shire's scratchpad: 99.84 + 12.00 cycles per mesh hop at 600 MHz (112-220 cycles, 186-366 ns), the same in both directions; 0.96 TB/s streaming from the shire 16 IDs away (2.1 hops on average) at 5.1 pJ/B (zeros) to 11.8 pJ/B (random).

Scratchpad address, format 0 (bit 30 = 0): 0x80000000 + (shire << 23) + offset, shire ID in bits 29:23, offset in bits 22:0; shire ID 0x7F means the requester's own shire. A request whose shire field is not the local shire goes out over the to_l3 mesh interface to the target shire.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.486 (§15.3); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.10, p.24 (§1.4.1.3); external/et-platform/et-common-libs/include/system/layout.h:71-76; docs/et-soc1-notes.md:88

statement: Scratchpad address, format 1 (bit 30 = 1, minions only): the shire ID sits in bits 29:28 and 10:6, so consecutive 64-byte lines land in different shires' scratchpads.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.486 (§15.3)

statement: Each shire's scratchpad is 2.5 MB (0x280000 in the firmware); 80 MB over the 32 compute shires.
page: Hand it to the next shire: on-chip relay vs DRAM

statement: Offset 0 of a shire's scratchpad faults; a global atomic through the local-scratchpad ID 0x7F is a bus error.
page: Hand it to the next shire: on-chip relay vs DRAM

statement: L3 hit: 110 + 12 cycles per mesh hop between the requesting shire and the line's home shire (fitted 110.5 + 11.99 on three cards); 159-169 cycles (265-282 ns) on average depending on the requesting shire.
A line's L3 home shire is PA[10:6]: consecutive 64-byte lines rotate over the 32 compute shires' L3 slices (default 'swizzle0'; the firmware leaves the swizzle register at reset).
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.24 (§1.4.1.2) and p.26-27 (§1.4.3); external/core-et/rtl/shire/esr/esr_cache_bank.v:88-103; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:373-377; memprobe: 1,500 lines, all but 2 within ±4 cycles of 110 + 12·hops(requester, PA[10:6]) (docs/et-soc1-notes.md:165)
note: The IDs are virtual shire IDs; a spare-shire remap would move them (NOC_Remap_Shires).

statement: Inside the home slice: L3 bank PA[12:11], sub-bank PA[14:13], set above.
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.24 (§1.4.1.2) and p.27 (Table 8, swizzle0); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:375

statement: The L3 is 32 MB: a 1 MB slice in each of the 32 compute shires, shared chip-wide and memory-side. The 5-bit home field means the master shire's cache is not an L3 home.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.13; driver_config.json `l3_kb` 32768; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.26 (five shire-ID bits for a 32-shire configuration)

statement: L3 streaming bandwidth: 0.98 TB/s on 1,024 minions at 600 MHz.
card: aifoundry2 (re-run on aifoundry2 and aifoundry3, within 1%)

statement: Reading from L3 costs 14.7 pJ per byte above idle [7.1-20.5].
Write-around stores coalesce in the L2's buffer and flush to the L3 once all four 16-byte qwords of a line are written (or on an explicit flush).

No coherence between caches: L1 data caches are not coherent; '…L' memory ops go straight to the local shire's L2, '…G' ops (and global atomics) go to the address's L3 home, and U-mode cache ops (EvictVA, FlushVA, PrefetchVA) move lines explicitly.
page: One hot line stops a shire

statement: A global atomic (amoaddg) is performed at the shire cache that homes the line. One contended line serialises at 10.00 cycles per atomic (about 60 M/s for the chip) and stops the host shire's own memory path; an uncontended remote global atomic round trip is 216 cycles.
page: One hot line stops a shire

statement: 16 LPDDR4X channels of 16 bits (256 bits in all): each memory shire drives two channels, and four LPDDR4X packages of four channels (64 bits each) sit on the card.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.17 (§1.5); external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf, pdf p.3; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4
note: The datasheet (pdf p.30) says two 16-bit PHYs share one 32-bit controller per memory shire; the firmware programs two uMCTL2 controller instances per memory shire (docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:286-287).

statement: 32 GB of LPDDR4X on these V3 cards (Micron part): 2 GB per channel; the chip supports 8 to 32 GB.
source: external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf, pdf p.1; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:289; external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.342 and p.552; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.30

statement: Datasheet rate: 4,266 MT/s, printed as 133 GB/s; 16 × 2 B × 4.266 GT/s is 136.5 GB/s (Esperanto's papers say 137).
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 (§1); docs/et-soc1-notes.md:20; docs/findings/05-claims.md:514

statement: The firmware hard-codes the 933 MHz DDR configuration on every card (controller clock 933 MHz, DRAM clock 1,866 MHz, 3,733 MT/s); telemetry reads mhz.ddr = 933 in every sample.
At 3,733 MT/s the 16 channels carry 119 GB/s.
Measured DRAM streaming bandwidth: 76 GB/s (about 64% of 119) on 1,024 minions at 600 MHz.
The 128,000 MB/s DRAM bandwidth the runtime reports is a placeholder constant in the service-processor firmware, not a measurement.
DRAM load: 287-297 cycles at 600 MHz (479-495 ns) depending on the requesting shire; the typical load from shire 0 is 299 cycles (500 ns), in each of 15 passes on three cards.
note: 287-297 is the pointer-chase plateau (memory-hierarchy page, requesters 0/7/24/31); 299 is the median of single loads to random lines from shire 0 (anatomy page).

statement: Past the L3, the DRAM leg costs 91 + 12 × hops(home shire, memory shire) cycles; about 25 of the 91 are the DRAM chip (activate 11, read and burst 14) and about 66 the memory shire. Only 25-28 of a ~300-cycle DRAM load are the DRAM's own timing.
source: docs/et-soc1-notes.md:166; docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json `decomp.ms_const`; cards.json `ms_const` (90-91 on three cards); docs/findings/05-claims.md:404

statement: The memory shire serving a line is PA[8:6] (so it is always the L3 home shire's low three bits) and the controller/channel within it is PA[9]: consecutive 64 B lines rotate over the 8 memory shires, the two channels alternate every 512 B.
source: external/et-platform/device-minion-runtime/tools/zebumem.c:67-72, 120-121; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.26-27 (§1.4.3: 'the Memory Shire is selected by the NoC using bits [8:6]'); confirmed by the memory shires' read counters (syscall 10), docs/et-soc1-notes.md:166

statement: Inside a channel: bank PA[12:10], column PA[17:13] (plus PA[5:1] within the line), row PA[18] and up (PA[34:18]); 8 banks, 2 KB page, one rank per channel.
note: Row/bank bits measured with one address bit flipped; the controller's ADDRMAP decode is the research agent's inference.

statement: Row state: an open-row hit saves 11 cycles (tRCD); a back-to-back conflict in the same bank, other row, adds about 37 cycles (36.5-37.4 on three cards). The controller runs an open-page policy: rows close at a refresh or another row's access, not on a timer.
Refresh every 2,325.4 cycles (3.88 µs at 600 MHz); a load caught in one waits up to 208 cycles. The firmware programs all-bank refresh (tRFCab 280.7 ns).

Controller configuration as programmed: open page, no auto-precharge, no power-down or self-refresh, no automatic ZQ, ECC off; tRCD = tRP = 18.2 ns, read latency 19.3 ns. DDR controller registers are service-processor only.
Reading from DRAM costs 114.6 pJ per byte above idle [89.0-141.3]; tensor loads of known data 94.6 pJ/B (zeros) and 132.6 pJ/B (random); a DRAM byte costs about 30× an own-scratchpad byte.
About 70% of a DRAM byte's energy lands on no metered rail (DDR PHY, I/O rail and the DRAM chips); no meter covers the memory shires or DRAM.
Each memory shire has a perf monitor with a 40-bit cycle counter (933 MHz) and two event counters; the firmware sets them to count mesh reads and writes, which U-mode can sample through syscall 10.

40-bit physical address space (1 TB): I/O 0x00_0000_0000 (1 GB), service processor 0x00_4000_0000 (1 GB), scratchpad 0x00_8000_0000 (2 GB), ESRs 0x01_0000_0000 (4 GB), PCIe 0x40_0000_0000 (256 GB), DRAM 0x80_0000_0000 (512 GB).
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.340 (Table 15-1); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.20 (§3)

statement: The DRAM region starts at 0x80_0000_0000; minions reach only the 'Low' view (M-mode low 8 MB, OS low to 0x80_FFFF_FFFF, memory low 0x81_0000_0000-0x87_FFFF_FFFF, 28 GB); device allocations come back as 0x80_xxxx_xxxx addresses.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.551 (Table 15-96) and p.553 (Table 15-98); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:348-350, 379-380

statement: ESR shire IDs (address bits 29:22): 0-33 minion shires, 232-239 memory shires 0-7, 253 the PCIe shire, 254 the I/O shire, 255 the local minion shire.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.487 (§15.4)

statement: Path of a cacheable load: an L1 miss sends Read_L2 over ET-Link to the local bank chosen by PA[7:6]; an L2 miss sends Read_L3 over the to_l3 mesh interface to the home shire's L3 slave chosen by PA[10:6] (data returns straight to the neighbourhood, before the fill); an L3 miss goes over to_sys to the memory shire chosen by PA[8:6], whose controller does activate/read/precharge.
note: A synthesis of the Shire Cache Specification and the RTL by the repo's research notes; the measured latency model (next fact) agrees.

statement: Measured load-to-use model from any requesting shire at 600 MHz: L1 5; L2 47-48; L3 110 + 12·hops(requester, home = PA[10:6]); DRAM 110 + 12·hops(requester, home) + 91 + 12·hops(home, memory shire = PA[8:6]). The mesh round trip is paid twice on a DRAM load: to the L3 home, then on to the memory shire.
source: docs/et-soc1-notes.md:164-166; anatomy page §1 'Trace one load' and headline tiles; docs/findings/05-claims.md:403-404 (V3 check: L3 within ±4 cycles for 99.4-99.97% of lines, DRAM within ±3 for 93-97%)
note: The route order inside the mesh was not measured.

statement: Host link: PCIe Gen4 x8 on an x16 card edge; the datasheet gives up to 128 Gbps each way (25.78 Gbit/s per lane PHY). 15.75 GB/s per direction is the Gen4 x8 figure; host transfer bandwidth was never measured here.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 (§1); external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf, pdf p.3; docs/findings/05-claims.md:489

statement: The PCIe dev card V3: ET-SoC-1 soldered down, 4 LPDDR4x devices (256-bit), 64 GB eMMC, USB (device/debug, OTG, FTDI UART), JTAG, 12 V input metered by an LTC4218 hot-swap controller.
source: external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf, pdf p.3 (Features) and pdf p.6-7 (Power Measurement)

statement: Regulators: minion and NoC share a TI TPSM831D31 (minion on a 3-phase output, 120 A max; NoC single-phase, 40 A max); the SRAM rail is an LTM4680 (60 A max).

The PMIC meters the 12 V input and three regulators (minion, NoC, SRAM); DDR, VDDQ, VDDQLP, PCIe logic, PCIe and Maxion rails have set points only. The service processor forwards a new value about every 133 ms (aifoundry2; 224 ms quiet pass on aifoundry3).
Governor thresholds in the firmware: 65 °C software temperature threshold and 65 W TDP; hardware catastrophic 75 °C and 75 W.
note: aifoundry3's boot service sets its TDP to 0, pinning it at 600 MHz.

statement: Operating points the firmware uses: 600 MHz at 517 mV, 700 MHz at 568 mV, 800 MHz at 618 mV (measured on die); every table in the reports is at 600 MHz, where a warm card sits.

statement: Boot minion clock 600 MHz on every card.

statement: Firmware DVFS limits: minion 300-800 MHz, NoC 300-500 MHz; the minion PLL table covers 300-1,400 MHz in 25 MHz steps.

statement: Design clocks: shire PLL output 1,000 MHz; a step clock of 400-1,000 MHz from PLL4 in the I/O shire; NoC clock 500 MHz from PLL2 in the I/O shire; reference oscillators 24 MHz and 100 MHz; the RISC-V mtime timer ticks at 10 MHz.
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.12 (Table 2); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.16 (§2.2.6), p.22 (§5.1.1), p.29 (§6.6.2.1)

statement: Minion rail: set point 520 mV, 516-518 mV on die under load at 600 MHz; per-shire 517-521 mV at idle. Firmware limits 400-620 mV (boot default 500).
SRAM rail (shire-cache arrays): set point 705 mV, 703-707 mV on die.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace-telemetry.jsonl (and horace2-, thermal-telemetry.jsonl: 3,681 samples, 20 Sep), fields `reg_mv.sram`, `die_mv.sram`; docs/findings/05-claims.md:41

statement: Other rails, set point / on die: DDR 800 / 762-768 mV, Maxion 600 / 583-586 mV, I/O shire - / 751-754 mV, PCIe shire - / 749-753 mV (PCIe logic set 775 mV), VDDQ 1,100 mV, VDDQLP 640 mV.
note: The firmware's boot default for the Maxion rail is 850 mV (thermal_pwr_mgmt.h:97); these cards run it at 600 mV.

statement: Per-shire on-die voltages at idle for all 34 minion shires (minion rail, SRAM, mesh, each as now/low/high) are in one file, keyed by the firmware's shire number.
note: Whether the pattern is a per-monitor offset was not settled (V3 TEL-Q INSUFFICIENT, 05-claims.md:568-571).

statement: Idle card after 20.6 h with no workload: 31.79 W at 73 °C, of which minion rail 11.05 W, SRAM 2.00 W, mesh 3.64 W and 15.10 W on no sensor.

note: Fitted (kind F in the claims index).

statement: fp32 TensorFMA on all 1,024 minions at 600 MHz and 80 °C, 9.18 TFLOPS: 38.29 W with zero operands, 46.73 W with ones, 63.40 W with random-normal data.
Fast local barrier: 32 barrier counters per shire, 8 bits wide (enough for all 64 harts), joined atomically with one CSR write (0x820) from user mode.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.327 (§10)

statement: Fast credit counters: two per hart (four per minion); any hart in any shire adds credits by writing a 64-bit mask to a shire's CREDINC0-3 ESRs; reading an empty counter blocks until a credit arrives.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.328 (§11)

statement: Measured at 600 MHz: shire barrier (FLB + credits, 32 minions) 232.5 cycles (388 ns); 32-minion allreduce 444 cycles (0.74 µs); 1,024-minion allreduce 1,393 cycles (2.3 µs); chip barrier from global atomics and credits 4,990-5,012 cycles (8.3 µs); credit round trip 140.2 + 14.4 cycles per hop (234 + 24 ns/hop), about 120 cycles blocking inside a shire.
Each allreduce tree level adds about one round trip: 68-71 cycles on the fast network (levels 0-2), 117 through the crossbar (levels 3-4) and 164-234 over the mesh (levels 5-9).
A flag handed through global atomics in memory costs 610-1,150 ns round trip (median 873), whatever the distance: it depends on which shire's L3 slice holds the flag's line.
source: on-chip communication page §'Latency grows with distance, except through memory'

statement: Aggregate message bandwidth with every minion sending 1 KB messages: 2,992 GB/s on tree-edge pairs, 1,120 GB/s in neighbourhood or shire rings, 87-156 GB/s across the mesh (7-34× less).
source: on-chip communication page table 'The numbers in the chart'; docs/et-soc1-notes.md:120

statement: Messaging energy per byte: 0.69 pJ/B on tree-edge pairs, 2.16 in a neighbourhood ring, 2.22 in a shire ring, and 9.2 + 1.75 pJ/B per mean hop across the mesh (busy cores included).

A multi-stage pipeline that hands each stage's output to the next shire's scratchpad runs about 12.4× faster than one that goes through DRAM (31× keeping it in the own scratchpad), at 116 / 8.9 / 4.3 pJ per byte moved (DRAM / next shire / own).

statement: Ridge points at 600 MHz (fp32 FLOP per byte fetched): own shire L2 or scratchpad 4, L3 or another shire's scratchpad 10, DRAM 130, PCIe 624 (unmeasured link).
